reference.title: Diamond Push-up
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press up.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s down, short pause, about 1.1 s up

prescription.progression: More reps, slower lowering, then feet elevated

cues.text: High plank with the hands together under the chest, thumbs and index fingers touching in a diamond.
Breathe in and lower the chest toward the diamond; elbows go back and slightly out.
Chest a few centimetres above the hands, body still one line.
Breathe out and press the floor away until the arms are straight.
Hold the plank at the top, then go again.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring straight out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Let them travel back at about 30-45 degrees from the body.
Place the diamond under the lower chest (sternum).
Brace the abs and squeeze the glutes.
Lower until the chest nearly touches the hands, or regress to the knees.

kinematics.norm: Thumbs and index fingers touching under the sternum; diamond hands gave the highest triceps and pectoralis activation of the hand positions tested (Intziegianni 2026; ACE triceps study ranked the triangle push-up first)
Arms straight but not locked at the top; elbows bend to about 90 degrees or more at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow tuck (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: Elbows close to the ribs, about 10-30 degrees from the body at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Head, trunk, hips and ankles (or knees) in one straight line throughout (clinical opinion)
Palms flat; the wrist bends back about 80-90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1 s up; lab studies used 2-2.5 s per repetition (Marcolin 2015)

sources.title: Intziegianni, Katsamis, Michaelides and Parpa 2026, electromyographic activation of the pectoralis major and triceps brachii during standard, diamond and wide hand position push-ups (Muscles 5(1):18)

Boehler, Porcari, Kline, Hendrix and Foster, ACE-sponsored research: best triceps exercises (American Council on Exercise; University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, 15 trained women, triceps EMG relative to the triangle push-up)
Kim, Kim and Ha 2016, effect of the push-up exercise at different palmar width on muscle activities (J Phys Ther Sci 28(2):446-449; PMC4792988)

Marcolin, Petrone, Moro, Battaglia, Bianco and Paoli 2015, selective activation of shoulder, trunk and arm muscles: a comparative analysis of different push-up variants (J Athl Train 50(11):1126-1132)

cautions: Wrist pain: the planted palm bends the wrist back about 80-90 degrees; use push-up handles or hex dumbbells to keep the wrists straight, or stop if pain persists (clinical opinion).
Elbow pain: the narrow hand position loads the elbows; widen the hands or regress to the knees (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Wrist discomfort: turn the diamond so the wrists are less twisted, or use a close grip with the hands a fist apart.
Too hard: knees down or hands on a bench.
